title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Guarantee System of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en:
Article 61 Where an existing account receivable is pledged, and the debtor of the account receivable confirms the authenticity of the account receivable to the pledgee but subsequently claims no liability on the ground that the account receivable does not exist or has been extinguished, the People's Court shall not support such a claim.
Where an existing account receivable is pledged, and the debtor of the account receivable does not confirm the authenticity of the account receivable, if the pledgee, naming the debtor of the account receivable as the defendant, requests priority satisfaction from the account receivable and can adduce evidence to prove that the account receivable was genuine at the time of registration of the pledge, the People's Court shall support the request; if the pledgee cannot adduce evidence to prove that the account receivable was genuine at the time of registration of the pledge and requests priority satisfaction from the account receivable solely on the ground that the pledge registration has been completed, the People's Court shall not support the request.
Where an existing account receivable is pledged, and the debtor of the account receivable has already performed the obligation to the creditor of the account receivable, if the pledgee requests the debtor of the account receivable to perform the obligation, the People's Court shall not support such a request, except where the debtor of the account receivable, after receiving a notice from the pledgee requesting performance to the pledgee, still performs the obligation to the creditor of the account receivable.
Where the right to income from infrastructure and public utility projects, claims arising from the provision of services or labor, or other future accounts receivable are pledged, and the parties establish a specific account for the account receivable, when a statutory or agreed event for the realization of the pledge occurs, if the pledgee requests priority satisfaction from the funds within such specific account, the People's Court shall support such a request; where the funds within the specific account are insufficient to discharge the debt or no specific account has been established, if the pledgee requests to have the future account receivable such as the right to project income valued by discount, or auctioned or sold, and obtain priority satisfaction from the proceeds, the People's Court shall support such a request in accordance with law.

Article 62 Where a debtor fails to perform an obligation that has become due, and a creditor, arising from the same legal relation, exercises a lien over a third party's chattel lawfully in its possession and claims priority satisfaction from the retained property, the People's Court shall support such a claim. Where the third party requests the return of the retained property on the ground that the retained property is not the debtor's property, the People's Court shall not support such a request.
Where the chattel retained between enterprises and the claim do not arise from the same legal relation, and the debtor requests the creditor to return the retained property on the ground that the claim is not a claim arising from the enterprise's ongoing business operations, the People's Court shall support such a request.
Where the chattel retained between enterprises and the claim do not arise from the same legal relation, and the creditor retains a third party's property, if the third party requests the creditor to return the retained property, the People's Court shall support such a request.
IV. Atypical Security

Article 63 Where a creditor and a security provider enter into a security contract stipulating the creation of security over a property right for which no provision has been made in laws or administrative regulations as being capable of securing an obligation, and a party claims that the contract is void, the People's Court shall not support such a claim. Where a party has not registered with the statutory registration authority in accordance with law and claims that such security has the effect of a real right, the People's Court shall not support such a claim.

Article 64 In a sale with retention of title, if the seller is legally entitled to reclaim the subject matter but fails to reach an agreement with the buyer through negotiation, and a party requests that the subject matter be auctioned or sold by referring to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on "cases for realizing security interest," the People's Court shall permit such request.
If the seller requests to reclaim the subject matter and this meets the requirements of Article 642 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support the request; if the buyer, by way of defense or counterclaim, argues for the auction or sale of the subject matter and the return of the surplus after deducting the unpaid price and necessary expenses, the People's Court shall handle the matter together.

Article 66 Where factoring, pledge of accounts receivable, and assignment of claims coexist over the same account receivable, and a party claims that the priority order shall be determined by referring to the provisions of Article 768 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support such a claim.
In factoring with recourse, if the factor initiates a lawsuit naming the creditor of the account receivable or the debtor of the account receivable as the defendant, the People's Court shall accept the case; if the factor initiates a lawsuit naming both the creditor of the account receivable and the debtor of the account receivable as defendants, the People's Court may accept the case.
After the creditor of the account receivable returns the principal and interest of the factoring financing to the factor or repurchases the claim of the account receivable, if the creditor requests the debtor of the account receivable to perform the obligation under the account receivable to it, the People's Court shall support such a request.

Article 67 In contracts such as sale with retention of title and financial leasing, the scope and effect of "bona fide third party" against whom the ownership of the seller or lessor, not being registered, may not be asserted, shall be handled by referring to the provisions of Article 54 of this Interpretation.

Article 68 Where a debtor or a third party agrees with a creditor to formally transfer property into the name of the creditor, such that if the debtor fails to perform an obligation that has become due, the creditor has the right to value the property by discount or to have the debt satisfied from the proceeds of auction or sale of the property, the People's Court shall find such agreement valid. Where the parties have completed the public notice formalities for the change in property rights, the People's Court shall support the creditor's request, made by referring to the relevant provisions of the Civil Code on security interests, for priority satisfaction from such property if the debtor fails to perform an obligation that has become due.
Where a debtor or a third party agrees with a creditor to formally transfer property into the name of the creditor, with the stipulation that if the debtor fails to perform an obligation that has become due, the property shall belong to the creditor, the People's Court shall find such agreement invalid, provided that the validity of the parties' expression of intent to provide security shall not be affected. Where the parties have completed the public notice formalities for the change in property rights, and the debtor fails to perform an obligation that has become due, the People's Court shall not support the creditor's request for ownership of the property; the People's Court shall support the creditor's request, made by referring to the provisions of the Civil Code on security interests, for priority satisfaction from the proceeds obtained by valuing the property by discount, or auctioning or selling it; after the debtor has performed the obligation, if the debtor requests the return of the property, or requests to have the debt satisfied from the proceeds obtained by valuing the property by discount, or auctioning or selling it, the People's Court shall support such a request.
Where a debtor agrees with a creditor to transfer property into the name of the creditor, with the stipulation that after a certain period, the debtor or a third party designated by the debtor shall repurchase it at the transaction principal plus a premium, and the debtor fails to perform the repurchase obligation when due, causing the property to belong to the creditor, the People's Court shall handle the matter by referring to the provisions of the second paragraph. If the subject of the repurchase did not exist from the outset, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 146 of the Civil Code, based on the legal relationship that was actually constituted.

Article 69 Where a shareholder provides security for the performance of a debt by transferring its equity interest into the name of a creditor, and the company or a creditor of the company requests the creditor, as the nominal shareholder, to bear joint and several liability with the shareholder on the ground that the shareholder has failed to fulfill or has not fully fulfilled its capital contribution obligation, or has fraudulently withdrawn its capital contribution, the People's Court shall not support such a request.

Article 70 Where a debtor or a third party, for the purpose of securing the performance of a debt, establishes a special margin account which is actually controlled by the creditor, or deposits its funds into a margin account established by the creditor, and the creditor claims priority satisfaction from the funds within the account, the People's Court shall support such a claim. Where a party claims, on the ground that the funds in the margin account fluctuate, that the creditor who actually controls the account does not have a right to priority satisfaction over the funds in the account, the People's Court shall not support such a claim.
A sub-account for margin established under a bank account shall be handled by referring to the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
If the agreed margin is not established for the purpose of securing the performance of a debt, or does not meet the circumstances set forth in the preceding two paragraphs, and the creditor claims priority satisfaction from the margin, the People's Court shall not support such a claim, provided that this does not affect the party's right to assert claims in accordance with the provisions of law or the agreement of the parties.
V. Supplementary Provisions
Article 71 This Interpretation shall come into force on January 1, 2021.
